evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Khamenei called the anti-government protests 'riots' and blamed the United States and Israel for trying to stop Iran's progress.
evidence.title: Iran’s Khamenei blames Israel, US in first comments on protests
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei called the anti-government protests 'riots' and blamed the United States and Israel for trying to stop Iran's progress.
evidence.source_locator: article body, quoted speech to graduating police cadets
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with direct contemporaneous quotation and clear date, but mediated through a secondary publisher.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct attribution to Khamenei in his role as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: He also said Mahsa Amini's death 'deeply broke my heart,' which is a limited sympathetic note but not restraint.
The speech was accusatory rather than protective and did not acknowledge state responsibility.

evidence.claim: Khamenei blamed protests on foreign 'enemies' seeking to overthrow the Islamic Republic and described them as psychological warfare against Iran.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei blames unrest on 'enemies' out to overthrow Islamic Republic
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei blamed protests on foreign 'enemies' seeking to overthrow the Islamic Republic and described them as psychological warfare against Iran.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting a direct quotation from Khamenei in the target year.
contrary_evidence: This was rhetoric about unrest, not a direct operational order.
The speech did not itself document killings or arrests.

evidence.claim: OHCHR recorded information concerning excessive and lethal force, live ammunition, arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial executions, unlawful killings, and internet disruption in response to the Amini protests.
evidence.title: Communication report: Iran (Islamic Republic of) IRN 23/2022
evidence.excerpt: OHCHR recorded information concerning excessive and lethal force, live ammunition, arbitrary arrests, torture, extrajudicial executions, unlawful killings, and internet disruption in response to the Amini protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN special-procedures communication summarizing a contemporaneous rights complaint.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-aligned security conduct under Khamenei's top-level authority.
contrary_evidence: This is a communication record, not a merits finding.
The page summarizes received allegations rather than a final adjudication.

evidence.claim: NetBlocks confirmed near-total internet disruption in parts of Kurdistan province and later nationwide platform and mobile-network restrictions during the Amini protests.
evidence.title: Internet disrupted in Iran amid protests over death of Mahsa Amini
evidence.excerpt: NetBlocks confirmed near-total internet disruption in parts of Kurdistan province and later nationwide platform and mobile-network restrictions during the Amini protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent network telemetry provider with contemporaneous measurements and clear protest linkage.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 protest onset and follow-on shutdowns
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Iranian authorities and their security councils, not a private Khamenei order transcript.
contrary_evidence: Connectivity was temporarily restored in some places, so this was not a uniform all-country blackout at every moment.
The report measures disruption, not the legal authority behind each order.

evidence.claim: HRW said Iranian security forces responded to widespread protests with excessive and lethal force, thousands were arrested, and authorities heavily disrupted internet access.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: ايران
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Iranian security forces responded to widespread protests with excessive and lethal force, thousands were arrested, and authorities heavily disrupted internet access.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the Persian country chapter
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Persian-language HRW summary of the 2022 record; broad but consistent with other independent accounts.
evidence.period_fit: Year-end synthesis of the 2022 protest cycle
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong attribution to the Iranian state under Khamenei.
contrary_evidence: This is a summary chapter rather than a case file.
It compresses many incidents into a broad overview.

evidence.claim: The mission concluded that Iran bore state responsibility for Jina Mahsa Amini's unlawful death and found serious violations against protesters, including a pattern of force, detentions, internet restrictions, sexual and gender-based violence, and killings; it recorded 551 people killed by September 2023, including 49 women and 68 children.
evidence.title: Report of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on the Islamic Republic of Iran
evidence.excerpt: The mission concluded that Iran bore state responsibility for Jina Mahsa Amini's unlawful death and found serious violations against protesters, including a pattern of force, detentions, internet restrictions, sexual and gender-based violence, and killings; it recorded 551 people killed by September 2023, including 49 women and 68 children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN investigative report with detailed methodology, state-responsibility findings, and quantified casualties.
evidence.period_fit: Post-period synthesis of the 16 Sept 2022 protest wave
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong state-level attribution under Khamenei's authority, though the report is not a personal command transcript.
contrary_evidence: The report is post-period and summarizes a year-long investigation rather than day-by-day 2022 contemporaneous reporting.
It does not isolate every action to Khamenei personally.

evidence.claim: Iran curbed access to Instagram and WhatsApp amid protests over Mahsa Amini's death; Reuters also reported NetBlocks data showing a nation-scale loss of connectivity and near-total disruption in parts of Kurdistan province.
evidence.title: As unrest grows, Iran restricts access to Instagram, WhatsApp
evidence.excerpt: Iran curbed access to Instagram and WhatsApp amid protests over Mahsa Amini's death; Reuters also reported NetBlocks data showing a nation-scale loss of connectivity and near-total disruption in parts of Kurdistan province.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire with direct technical corroboration from NetBlocks and multiple local-resident reports.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the September 2022 protest crackdown.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Iranian authorities; Khamenei attribution is structural through his supreme authority over the security apparatus, not a direct order shown in this article.
contrary_evidence: Iran's minister of communications said earlier on Wednesday he had been misquoted after news outlets cited him as saying the authorities might disrupt internet services for security reasons.

evidence.claim: OFAC designated seven senior leaders in Iran's government and security apparatus for shutting down internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters after Mahsa Amini's death; the release also named the communications minister and cyber-police chief as responsible for blocking Internet access and monitoring users.
evidence.title: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Leaders Responsible for Internet Shutdown and Violent Crackdown on Peaceful Protests
evidence.excerpt: OFAC designated seven senior leaders in Iran's government and security apparatus for shutting down internet access and continuing violence against peaceful protesters after Mahsa Amini's death; the release also named the communications minister and cyber-police chief as responsible for blocking Internet access and monitoring users.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary sanctions action naming officials and describing the conduct they were designated for.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The press release attributes conduct to senior state/security officials, not personally to Khamenei, but the conduct falls within his structural command over the security state.
contrary_evidence: The document is a sanctions finding, not a court judgment, and it does not prove a personal Khamenei order.

evidence.claim: CPJ said at least 28 journalists had been arrested as clashes between security forces and protesters left dozens dead, with arrests taking place amid an internet blackout and major disruptions to phone and social media networks.
evidence.title: Iranian security forces step up arrests of journalists amid anti-state protests
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said at least 28 journalists had been arrested as clashes between security forces and protesters left dozens dead, with arrests taking place amid an internet blackout and major disruptions to phone and social media networks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Leading press-freedom NGO using multiple in-country sources and contemporaneous reporting; claim is specific and time-bounded.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the September 2022 protest wave.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Iranian security forces; Khamenei attribution is indirect through supreme-leader control of the coercive apparatus.
contrary_evidence: CPJ's count depends on in-country sources and media reports because access was constrained by the blackout.

evidence.claim: RSF said at least 33 journalists were in jail, while Iranian authorities were summoning and threatening journalists and ordering them to stop publishing protest coverage on their outlets and social networks.
evidence.title: Iran: at least 33 journalists in jail while the world marks Access to Information Day
evidence.excerpt: RSF said at least 33 journalists were in jail, while Iranian authorities were summoning and threatening journalists and ordering them to stop publishing protest coverage on their outlets and social networks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dedicated press-freedom watchdog report with named journalists and specific interference methods.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Iranian authorities; the report does not itself identify a direct Khamenei order, but the conduct fits the apparatus under his control.
contrary_evidence: RSF relies on its sources and reports; it is not a judicial finding.

evidence.claim: NetBlocks confirmed a near-total disruption to internet service in parts of Kurdistan province, followed by national restrictions on Instagram and WhatsApp and a nation-scale shutdown of mobile networks during the protest period.
evidence.title: Internet disrupted in Iran amid protests over death of Mahsa Amini
evidence.excerpt: NetBlocks confirmed a near-total disruption to internet service in parts of Kurdistan province, followed by national restrictions on Instagram and WhatsApp and a nation-scale shutdown of mobile networks during the protest period.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Technical network measurement is strong for connectivity effects and dates, though not for legal responsibility.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, starting the day after Amini-related protests escalated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Connectivity effects are attributable to state action only indirectly; the report measures disruption, not command responsibility, which must be inferred from the state context.
contrary_evidence: NetBlocks measures network disruption, not the legal order that caused it.

evidence.claim: The Human Rights Council condemned the violent crackdown on peaceful protests in Iran, saying it had caused hundreds of deaths including dozens of children and thousands of arrests, and created an independent fact-finding mission to investigate the violations.
evidence.title: Human Rights Council establishes fact-finding mission to investigate alleged human rights violations in Iran related to the protests that began on 16 September 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Human Rights Council condemned the violent crackdown on peaceful protests in Iran, saying it had caused hundreds of deaths including dozens of children and thousands of arrests, and created an independent fact-finding mission to investigate the violations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN meeting summary of a Council resolution directly addressing the protest crackdown.
evidence.period_fit: Same 2022 protest wave; resolution adopted in November 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directed at the Iranian state apparatus rather than Khamenei personally; however the crackdown falls within his supreme-leader authority over security institutions.
contrary_evidence: The resolution is a political and investigative step, not a final adjudication of individual criminal liability.

evidence.claim: HRW said Iranian authorities used partial or total internet shutdowns during the protests and blocked WhatsApp and Instagram since September 21, 2022, by order of Iran's National Security Council, while arresting thousands of protesters and hundreds of students, defenders, journalists, and lawyers.
evidence.title: Iran: UN Rights Council Should Create Fact-Finding Mission
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Iranian authorities used partial or total internet shutdowns during the protests and blocked WhatsApp and Instagram since September 21, 2022, by order of Iran's National Security Council, while arresting thousands of protesters and hundreds of students, defenders, journalists, and lawyers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major rights NGO summarizing contemporaneous abuses and citing a specific state order for platform blocks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The cited order is to the National Security Council, not personally to Khamenei, but the policy sits under the supreme-leader system he heads.
contrary_evidence: HRW's account is advocacy-based and partly based on survivor accounts; the exact chain of command is not fully exposed.
